Yes. The main options are:

• Eyeglasses: the frame itself for everyday wear.
• Prescription lenses: lenses made to your vision needs.
• Clip-on styles: regular glasses with a sun clip for indoor and outdoor use.
• Sunglasses: tinted eyewear for sun protection.

For lenses, the simplest breakdown is:
• Single vision: one correction across the whole lens.
• Progressive: distance, intermediate, and near correction in one lens.
• Polycarbonate: lightweight, impact-resistant lenses with built-in UV protection.
• Blue light filtering: helps reduce blue light from screens.
• Anti-reflective coating: cuts glare and reflections.
• Tinted or polarized options: turns them into sun-ready lenses.

If you want the easiest starting point, everyday eyeglasses with polycarbonate single vision lenses are a great first choice. Do you need glasses for distance, reading, or both?
